#1668. Man United dealt MAJOR blow with Benjamin Sesko set to be ruled out until January - leaving struggling club with NO fit striker - as problems mount for under-fire Michael Carrick

Published: 16:32 EDT, 28 October 2026 | Updated: 19:21 EDT, 28 October 2026

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko is set to be ruled out until at least January with a shin injury.

The 23-year-old was struggling with the issue at the beginning of the season and saw his game time carefully managed as the club attempted to nurse him back to full fitness, but those efforts now appear to have been in vain.

Sesko has not featured for the club since their defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup on September 16, when he was substituted in the 66th minute.

He missed all of pre-season with the complaint, which also plagued him last season and resurfaced against Liverpool in May, causing him to miss the final three Premier League games.

The Slovenian, who pulled out of international duty last month, now looks set to be sidelined until the new year, dealing a major blow to United during a difficult run of form and leaving Michael Carrick without a recognised striker.

Right winger Bryan Mbeumo has been filling in at No 9, starting their last five games there in all competitions, with Carrick having lost faith in Dutchman Joshua Zirkzee.

Sesko was struggling with the issue at the beginning of the season and saw his game time limited as the club worked to ensure a full comeback

Since joining United from RB Leipzig in a deal worth £73.7million in August 2025, Sesko has made 38 appearances in all competitions, scoring 14 goals and recording one assist.

In regard to this campaign, he has scored once in six appearances across all competitions, against Everton in the Premier League.

He will now miss crucial Premier League games, including meetings with Liverpool and Arsenal, as well as at least three Champions League matches.

United are currently languishing in 16th place in the Premier League, one point clear of the relegation zone.

They face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge this weekend after Carrick held clear-the-air talks with captain Bruno Fernandes on Wednesday following the midfielder's criticism of the manager's tactics after the defeat by Como.

United were beaten 4-1 in the Champions League last Wednesday and Fernandes criticised the decision not to press man-to-man against the Italian side, saying it allowed their opponents to grow in confidence.

Asked whether Carrick had got things wrong tactically, the 32-year-old midfielder said: 'That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me.'

Carrick dropped Fernandes to the bench against Bournemouth and then left him there while bringing on four other substitutes, including teenager Shea Lacey.

Afterwards, Fernandes was among the United players targeted for abuse by fans as they made a public show of support for Carrick before turning on the team.

The Portugal midfielder appeared to respond with a veiled dig at Carrick on Sunday night when he liked a cryptic Instagram post that read: 'Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care.'

With Fernandes set to return to the line-up at Stamford Bridge, there was more positive news for United after Kobbie Mainoo resumed training at Carrington on Wednesday.

#1666. Liverpool transfer news: Reds mull surprise plan to bring Alexander-Arnold home

By Axel Clody | 02 Nov 2026 07:08

Trent Alexander-Arnold is struggling at Real Madrid this season, and Liverpool are thinking about signing him, via a rather surprising option, according to the Spanish press.

With his line-up against Barcelona (2-1), Jose Mourinho disowned Real Madrid’s summer transfer business, sending Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold to the bench in favour of midfielder Federico Valverde.

Although the boss supports his two full-backs publicly, the question of a departure arises for the 28-year-old Englishman in particular, as he is wanted by Liverpool and Chelsea, among others.

According to Cadena SER, however, Liverpool have a surprising plan for their former player.

The outlet says that the Premier League’s current fifth-placed side is considering offering Real Madrid a loan for their number 14 this winter.

Admittedly, Alexander-Arnold is playing little in Spain this season, with seven games and one assist, and is third choice in his position. But what would be the Spanish club’s interest in sending the former Liverpool man away via a deal that would not be permanent and would bring in little money?

Unlike Endrick (20), sent to Lyon last year and again on his way out in January via a loan, the right-back would have no future at Real Madrid afterwards if he moved in January 2027, because his age (28) does not suggest that his progress will be on the rise.

All in all, if there is a loan, this temporary transfer will need to include a compulsory option to buy. Otherwise, the Spanish side will have no interest in parting with Trent Alexander-Arnold.

While Real Madrid signed the 36-cap international for a minimal sum (£8.5m) in 2025, a few weeks before the end of his contract at Liverpool, a sale for a reasonable amount would in any case guarantee the Spanish club a profit, despite the fall in Alexander-Arnold’s market value, now estimated at around £51m.

According to Marca, the right-back is not considering leaving the club for the moment. But Real Madrid’s interest in Spain’s Pedro Porro (Tottenham), who is also targeted by Barcelona, should not reassure him about his sporting and personal future in the Spanish capital.

An offer from Liverpool, or Chelsea, could speed up the matter, provided that the deal is permanent: it is hard to see Real Madrid wanting to keep Trent Alexander-Arnold in their squad beyond January 2027, if a move happens.

#1665. Report: 'Frustrating' verdict on Liverpool recent transfer business

Richard Hughes arrived at Liverpool to lead the post-Jurgen Klopp shakeup.

Appointed sporting director in 2024 the Scots exec had made his reputation at Bournemouth. His first transfer window was quiet - doing a deal for Federico Chiesa - but he had some success in tying down Virgil van Dijk and Mohamed Salah to new contracts.

Following Liverpool’s Premier League title win under Slot in 2024/25 Hughes set about reordering the squad. He cleared out several top stars - including Darwin Nunez and Luis Diaz - and also failed to get a new deal over the line for Trent Alexander-Arnold.

The Anfield side spent around £450m that summer - on players like Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Hugo Ekitike and others - but got worse.

LFC unravel under Richard HughesArne Slot paid with his job with Hughes overseeing the appointment of Andoni Iraola as a replacement. He stayed in place for the summer 2026 transfer window - losing Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate on frees - and spending big once again on Bradley Barcola. By the time the window closed it appeared as though Iraola had a squad with gaps everywhere - with no suitable right winger to replace Salah. Now it’s emerged that the club have been left “frustrated” with Hughes’ spending - transfer campaigns which have damaged the quality in the squad that Iraola has to work with.

Arne Slot paid with his job with Hughes overseeing the appointment of Andoni Iraola as a replacement.

Liverpool 'frustrated' by Richard Hughes transfer spending That’s according to a report in the Athletic which claims that the club have got a job on their hands to correct the errors of the recent past. “There has been frustration with areas of Liverpool’s recruitment in recent years that has left Andoni Iraola working with a small, unbalanced squad,” the report reads. “He is managing it well so far, losing just one of his first 12 games in charge, but additional expertise in the scouting department will hopefully help Liverpool to identify more players who can enhance the squad further.” Hughes left Liverpool following the conclusion of the summer transfer window - pitching up at Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia. In years gone by, the derby was a result to skip over for Milan. It was a defeat waiting to happen and it seemingly couldn’t be changed and then it flipped. Matteo Gabbia’s goal stopped the streak and in turn, it started a new one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri entered last night’s game with a run of seven unbeaten and they finished the night with eight unbeaten and a fourth consecutive win. It’s a first in itself for more than 50 years, which is telling.

It’s a result which brought Gerry Cardinale to tears and it’s clear that something has really clicked at San Siro, as the player ratings showed.

Speaking at a press conference after the game, as relayed by MilanNews, the Inter coach spoke about several things, including his unfavourable record in the Derby della Madonnina.

“Compared to last year, there’s something to note about our approach to matches: the superficiality and casualness with which we handle certain situations, where we lack a bit of grit, a bit of determination, a bit of danger perception. But we need to rediscover them.

“We need to be aware that right now, despite a few more points than last year, we’ve lost something that absolutely needs to be rediscovered.”

“I couldn’t, because the forwards have had some problems in the last few days. Bonny only made himself available on the last day after two days with a fever of 39°C and severe nausea and vomiting, so we were forced to find a solution, to make a virtue of necessity, changing the system a bit.

“We knew that, in this type of match, it would be the right thing to have pace on the wings with Spence and Carlos and attack the line a bit more, as well as looking for depth in space with Diouf operating under the striker, looking for both him and Sucic between the lines.

“Unfortunately, sometimes things don’t work out, but, I repeat, we were forced to change.”

“It’s too easy to talk now that Lautaro is injured and the other two forwards aren’t feeling well. These things happen, fortunately not often. We’ll make some assessments, but we’re still happy with our four forwards, in addition to what Lavelli gives us, what Mosconi gives us, and whoever we bring in from the Under 23s.

“But, I repeat, it’s too easy to bring these things up at a time when two forwards aren’t at their best and the third is injured.”

Is there something mental that comes into play in the derby?

“There’s always something mental, I think, and history teaches us this, when you get to play another season after winning.

“So, let’s try not to throw everything away and try to rediscover some determination, some humility in doing certain things, starting with myself, because I’m primarily responsible for everything we do.

“We shouldn’t throw everything away because we’ve reached the tenth matchday and this is the first game we’ve lost. We’ve got 25 points, and last year we’d got fewer, but we’ve always been able to react, we’ve always kept our feet on the ground and our heads down to build a strong season.

“That’s what we’d like to do again this year, because we have this desire and this ambition to have another strong season; we just need to find the way to build it again.”

#1662. Opinion: Sensational, The Premier League's most important star is officially Liverpool's

Liverpool boast the Premier League's most important player right now. What an incredible season he's having so far.

Things felt like an absolute mess at Liverpool heading into the summer and they didn't exactly feel tidy coming out of it. That's not because the Reds didn't have good players, nor were they even in a Manchester United kind of mess.

The problem was that Liverpool had a title winning team in 2025 and then proceeded to spend an awful lot of money tearing it up. Record-breaking amounts went out on players but none delivered. If we're honest, we're still waiting to see a return for the cash.

Of course, when you've got players this good, you can only do so badly. A 'poor' season for Liverpool is still one where they qualify for European football - but the money spent means the standards are sky high.

You want to see these players delivering at the absolute elite level, something that simply didn't happen over the 2025/26 campaign. But we might finally be seeing it.

The Alexander Isak showLiverpool made Isak the most expensive player in English football history in 2025 when they bought him from Newcastle United. His first season, however, was a disaster. Isak had essentially skipped pre-season in an effort to force the transfer, meaning he arrived at Liverpool half-fit. That's probably an exaggeration, actually - he was barely fit at all. By the time he finally got going, he broke his leg. It meant that Liverpool's record signing provided a grand total of three Premier League goals in his debut season. A figure he has already doubled in this campaign with his six coming in just seven fixtures.

Liverpool made Isak the most expensive player in English football history in 2025 when they bought him from Newcastle United. His first season, however, was a disaster.

Isak had essentially skipped pre-season in an effort to force the transfer, meaning he arrived at Liverpool half-fit. That's probably an exaggeration, actually - he was barely fit at all. By the time he finally got going, he broke his leg.

It meant that Liverpool's record signing provided a grand total of three Premier League goals in his debut season. A figure he has already doubled in this campaign with his six coming in just seven fixtures.

But more importantly, it's when Isak has scored the goals that really catches the eye. They've come in five different matches and have directly delivered seven points across the campaign. Only two other players can match that: Erling Haaland and Nicolas Jackson.

Strip those points away and Liverpool drop all the way down to 16th on eight points. That's so low that they're only barely still ahead of Manchester United (17th in the Premier League table on seven points after nine (9) matches).

This is ultimately why Liverpool paid the money. Isak is proving himself to be incredibly decisive, bagging his goals across multiple games and in important ways, rather than hat tricks in 6-0 drubbings.

Finally, Liverpool's 2025 rebuild might be clicking together and reaching the standards it called for.

#1661. Arsenal make Premier League history by doing something no side has ever done to Liverpool at Anfield

By Lewis Blain | 02 Nov 2026 07:21

Arsenal strengthened their position at the top of the Premier League with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield.

Kai Havertz's first-half goal proved decisive, but Mikel Arteta's side also delivered another outstanding defensive performance.

In fact, the Gunners achieved something no visiting team had ever managed against Liverpool at Anfield in Premier League history.

According to The xG Philosophy, Arsenal conceded just 0.00 expected goals on target (xGOT) against Liverpool, a record low for a visiting team at Anfield in the Premier League era.

The statistic underlines the effectiveness of Arteta's defensive unit, particularly given the pressure Liverpool applied during the opening stages.

Arsenal took the lead in the 16th minute when Declan Rice delivered a dangerous ball across the face of goal, allowing Havertz to convert at the back post.

No team had ever done this to Liverpool at Anfield in Premier League history.

Liverpool responded with sustained pressure, with goalkeeper David Raya producing an important intervention to prevent Virgil van Dijk's flick-on from reaching Alexander Isak. Florian Wirtz also struck the crossbar with a free-kick as the hosts searched for an equaliser.

However, the Gunners' defensive organisation improved considerably after the interval, restricting Liverpool's opportunities and ensuring Raya was rarely seriously troubled.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's introduction helped the champions regain control late on, while Alisson denied Christos Tzolis a second goal with an excellent save.

The result secured Arsenal's first Premier League victory at Anfield since 2012 and moved them three points clear at the summit.

There is no doubt that Arsenal deserve enormous credit for their defensive display, but Liverpool's attacking numbers will concern Andoni Iraola.

The Reds have registered just 13.3 expected goals (xG) in the Premier League this season, ranking tenth in the division, while their 12 big chances created leave them joint-19th. They also rank eighth for touches inside the opposition box, ninth for shots on target per match and joint bottom for set-piece goals, having failed to score from one.

Alexander Isak has managed six goals in eight league appearances, but the striker has received limited service, while big-money signings Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola have yet to deliver consistent end product.

Arsenal's defensive structure undoubtedly contributed to those struggles, but Liverpool cannot rely on facing opponents who allow them to create opportunities through sustained pressure.

Iraola's attacking approach has shown promise, particularly with the pace and intensity of their high press, but the lack of quality in the final third is becoming increasingly difficult to overlook.

Against Arsenal, the Gunners' defensive excellence was the main story. However, Liverpool's inability to turn promising attacking positions into genuine chances suggests there is still plenty of work for Iraola to do.

#1660. Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Defensive rebuilding is next summer’s big project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

United were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

“There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick said. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”

There was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

He recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

Asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He showed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

“There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”

Speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

“But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ

The hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

“Scoring before half-time is always important if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV

Dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

Man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

The Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

Mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

The Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb

What a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

Wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

Some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you…

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa

Enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

We are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

Ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

End-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ

There will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

You would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

And United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

What a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

Davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

There’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second big save from Lammens. United look a threat going forward but then so do Ipswich, who are picking their moments to break and doing so well.

Rashford tries his luck from long range with a knuckle-ball free-kick. He doesn’t get any accuracy on the strike and it harmlessly flies off target.

This game has exploded into life in the last couple of minutes. End to end action. Scherpen first denying Dalot, then Ipswich going straight down the other end from a long punted clearance and Enciso, holding off Shaw and Mbeumo, forcing a save from Lammens. In keeping with the basketball nature of things, United then went back up the other end, with Cunha overhitting a cross for the onrushing Rashford before Fernandes’ goalbound shot is blocked. It’s certainly entertaining.

Chances at both ends! Firstly, Emersonn hacks Man Utd’s corner away, and Enciso uses his blistering speed to outpace Shaw and Mbeumo, creating a one-on-one with Lammens, who does excellently to smother the shot. Then Man Utd then fly forward straight away and Cunha fires a low delivery across the six-yard box which is marginally out of Rashford’s reach.

Man Utd counter as Fernandes releases Mbeumo with a ball over the top. The hosts recycle the ball well after Rashford crosses, allowing Dalot to cut in or his left foot and bend a curler for the far corner. Scherpen uses every inch of his towering frame to make an eye-catching diving save.

Maeda shows a great turn of pace to breeze past Mbeumo and reach the byline. Under pressure from Dalot, the winger hits his near post cross into Lammens’ hands.

Again, Rashford runs at Ipswich’s backline and cuts inside to reach the penalty area. He tees up Cunha, who smashes an effort well over the bar.

Martinez attempts an ambitious switch of play, aiming for Maguire, but boots the ball straight out of play. O’Shea and Shaw then both go up for a header, with the Ipswich man coming off worse and staying on the ground. He’s back on his feet now and play resumes.

There’s an early roar from the Old Trafford crowd as Rashford gets on the ball and sprints at Ipswich captain O’Shea, who is playing at right back.

Old Trafford welcomes both sides. Can Man Utd find their first win of the Premier League season or will Ipswich spoil the party?

Carlos Baleba has walking out on to the pitch after being introduced at Old Trafford. The new £70m signing from Brighton has been posing for pictures with a shirt and applauding all sections of the ground. He won’t be in action for another two or three weeks most likely owing to an existing ankle injury.

Carlos Baleba is introduced to the Manchester United fans! 👋 pic.twitter.com/QHTCkpe5dz

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of both line-ups.

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

"He's a fantastic footballer." Ashley Young discusses Marcus Rashford 🔊 pic.twitter.com/4hYAtx9zZF

Michael Carrick explains the changes to his Man Utd starting XI to face Ipswich 🔴Watch the game live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/p9FD36h3OM

Against Hull, Man Utd’s forward line looked way off the pace. In an attempt to stop history repeating itself, Michael Carrick has turned to Marcus Rashford, who is making his first start for the club since the end of 2024.

When Rashford last featured for Man Utd, he was wearing the No.10 shirt. That is now occupied by Mathues Cunha who starts as the central frontman, with Rashford now sporting the No.9.

The hosts will also need captain Bruno Fernandes to deliver. He will levels below his exceptionally high standards last time out, while Bryan Mbeumo also needs to make more of an impact.

It was short and not sweet. Playing in their first top-flight campaign since 2001-02, Ipswich finished 19th with just 22 points under Kieran McKenna.

This time, Gary O’Neil is the boss and they’ve already ticked off one victory thanks to those three points against Sunderland.

Is he the man to guide Ipswich to safety?

Martinez and Dalot are two alterations in Man Utd’s backline, replacing Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui. Gary Neville feels the club’s defence could let them down this season.

"You can get at them" ❌Gary Neville has concerns over Manchester United's defence for the upcoming season particularly after defeat to Hull 🤔 pic.twitter.com/v3sEjInI2j

First game of the season at Old Trafford for United and one they really need to win after last weekend’s shock defeat at newly promoted Hull City.

Summer signing Andrey Santos has made way for Kobbie Mainoo to partner Youri Tielemans in attack and it’ll be really interesting to see how that midfield pairing dovetail.

It’s a first start at Old Trafford since December 2024 for Marcus Rashford in an attacking looking side. Matheus Cunha is likely to operate as a false nine.

There’s going to be an onus on Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo to provide pace and penetration from out wide and get in behind Ipswich’s defence.

Ipswich enjoyed a great start back in the top flight by winning their opening game against Sunderland and will be out to build on that victory.

Against Hull, Michael Carrick opted for a midfield pivot of Man Utd debutants Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. However, the pair were completely overran by Hull’s intensity and energy.

Carrick has turned to Kobbie Mainoo as the resolution, with the 21-year-old replacing Andrey Santos. Mainoo went to the World Cup with England this summer, but didn’t play a single minute.

A return to Old Trafford will give Mainoo a chance to remind everyone of his quality.

"I wouldn't say massive concerns, but he will be worried""If Carrick doesn't see a reaction today, there is a problem"The Manchester United players will be under pressure to perform, says Ashley Young 📈 pic.twitter.com/dR6uat4l2P

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

Gary O’Neil has named an unchanged line-up from the side that beat Sunderland last week. Recent signing Exequiel Palacios is on the bench after joining from Bayer Leverkusen.

Your Town at Old Trafford! ✊ pic.twitter.com/mVMj2LVNvs

Unsurprisingly, Michael Carrick has shuffled his pack after last weekend’s disastrous defeat to Hull. Rashford, Mainoo, Martinez and Dalot all come into the starting X1.

📍 Home.Back where we belong. https://t.co/VbvwRcdF4t pic.twitter.com/37rThnGjyN

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

Man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

When the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

Reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick said: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

“So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”

Against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1659. Tottenham transfer news: Forgotten £50m outcast now given fresh hope of Spurs escape in January

By Lewis Blain | 02 Nov 2026 07:43

Richarlison could finally be handed a route out of Tottenham Hotspur after Trabzonspor renewed their interest in signing the Brazilian forward.

The 29-year-old has fallen out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi and has been left outside the club's first-team plans following a frustrating summer transfer window.

With Spurs now reportedly willing to accept a reduced fee, January could represent their final opportunity to secure a transfer before his contract expires.

According to reports in Turkey (via Sport Witness), Trabzonspor have not given up on signing Richarlison and could make another attempt during the January transfer window.

It is reported that the Turkish side are considering a renewed approach, although they must first create space in their foreign-player quota.

Ruslan Malinovskyi and Paul Onuachu are among the players who could make way, with Trabzonspor's financial position and squad planning also likely to influence their decision.

Galatasaray are understood to be interested too, with both Turkish clubs working behind the scenes to explore a potential deal.

Tottenham are reportedly prepared to accept around €10m (£8.5m) in January, significantly less than the €20m (£17m) they requested during the summer. That represents a considerable reduction for a player who cost Spurs around £50m, but his situation has become increasingly difficult.

Richarlison has failed to secure a move despite interest from England, Turkey and Brazil, and De Zerbi has subsequently left him outside his core plans, with the forgotten forward restricted to involvement with the U21s.

Spurs also reportedly missed out on signing Marseille's Amine Gouiri because they were unable to offload either Richarlison or Dominic Solanke.

Richarlison's Tottenham career has become a frustrating combination of inconsistent performances, failed transfers and a breakdown in his relationship with the club.

The Brazilian has struggled to establish himself as the first-choice striker, while public disagreements over his future have further complicated matters.

He reportedly rejected the opportunity to sign a contract extension, leaving Spurs facing the prospect of losing him for nothing when his deal expires in summer 2027.

Several potential exits collapsed during the summer, including interest from former club Everton and Brazilian side Vasco da Gama, while his exclusion from De Zerbi's plans has left him in limbo.

A January departure now appears increasingly sensible for all parties. Tottenham can recover a modest fee, Richarlison can pursue regular first-team football, and De Zerbi can move on from a difficult situation.

Trabzonspor still have obstacles to overcome, but the reduced asking price could finally make an agreement possible.

#1657. Opinion: Insane Trent Alexander-Arnold Liverpool return moves one step closer, story out of Real Madrid hints at it

Trent Alexander-Arnold's future is up in the air right now. A move to Liverpool looks a lot more likely after recent comments out of Real Madrid.

Trent Alexander-Arnold didn't exactly shock the football world when he left Liverpool for Real Madrid in 2025 but it was certainly one of the biggest moves in recent times. A homegrown Reds deciding to move away from the club, using the end of his contract to sign for Los Blancos.

It's a story we've seen before. Twice, ridiculously enough.

Steve McManaman did it back in 1999 as one of the very first major players to take advantage of the Bosman ruling. Though, Liverpool were a bit of a mess at the time and certainly not looking capable of challenging for the top honours.

Michael Owen in 2004, however, was a massive blow. He didn't really leave on a free but entered the final year of his contract while refusing to sign a new one. That forced a cut-price move for Liverpool's most valuable player, who joined Real Madrid for a pittance.

Fast-forward to 2025 and Alexander-Arnold did exactly the same thing. The Reds got a small fee for a fraction of his value and lost him to Madrid.

And yet, there's a sense that he might be the first of the three to actually head back the other way. Especially as it might just suit all parties.

Trent Alexander-Arnold to LiverpoolAlexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid with dreams of the Ballon d'Or. It doesn't feel too much to say that it's all turned into a nightmare. The Scouser just doesn't play. He's appeared in just six of a possible 10 La Liga fixtures, starting a mere three of those. It's 266 minutes total out of a possible 900. And now Jose Mourinho is making it clear that this is purely preference. There's competition for places at right-back and Alexander-Arnold is not first choice. Or second. "[The situation with Alexander-Arnold] hurts me, said Mourinho. "Our squad planning was to have 2 players in each position, and now I'm playing a 3rd guy in their place [Fede Valverde], and that really makes me sad.

Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid with dreams of the Ballon d'Or. It doesn't feel too much to say that it's all turned into a nightmare.

The Scouser just doesn't play. He's appeared in just six of a possible 10 La Liga fixtures, starting a mere three of those. It's 266 minutes total out of a possible 900.

And now Jose Mourinho is making it clear that this is purely preference. There's competition for places at right-back and Alexander-Arnold is not first choice. Or second.

"[The situation with Alexander-Arnold] hurts me, said Mourinho.

"Our squad planning was to have 2 players in each position, and now I'm playing a 3rd guy in their place [Fede Valverde], and that really makes me sad.

"In this very specific situation, I think it's better for the team to play Fede there. I consider Fede a more offensive right-back than the other two right now.

"We explained this situation to Trent and [Denzel] Dumfries, and they both accepted it as they understood it's what best for the team right now.

Maybe everyone will play eventually but right now it's Alexander-Arnold who's missing out. Dumfries has started five of their 10 La Liga fixtures, playing in eight.

Understandably, then, speculation continues that Alexander-Arnold will leave the club and his reputation will absolutely develop intense interest in him from major clubs. But once you look at the elite clubs in need of a right-back, one stands out: Liverpool.

Jeremie Frimpong, essentially signed as Alexander-Arnold's replacement, has not worked out and they don't currently have a natural right-back. Ronald Araujo plays there but he's really a centre-back, even if he's playing very well.

His attacking output is minimal - a dramatic difference to when Alexander-Arnold was there.

Mourinho's admittance that the player is out of the team because he's just not preferred there is a proper admittance that Alexander-Arnold is surplus to requirements. Real Madrid won't let that situation continue, given his wages and value.

A move is getting closer, then. And it's to Liverpool that makes the most sense.

#1656. Rangers' Tynecastle escape cannot hide familiar flaws in McInnes' side

Published: 18:21 EDT, 28 October 2026 | Updated: 19:47 EDT, 28 October 2026

Less than a week ago, following another defeat in Europe, Celtic manager Martin O’Neill found himself fending off criticisms his side is a Jekyll and Hyde outfit.

His opposite number in the blue half of Glasgow, Derek McInnes, ought to be equally concerned about that label getting slapped on the heads of his players in the wake of a messy performance at Tynecastle that ended with an ill-deserved point.

His team got away with it thanks to Olwethu Makhanya’s late header. Celtic slipping up at home to Dundee United helped too. That, though, should not disguise the glaring problems with this display and the questions they raise over Rangers’ ability to keep the pedal to the metal.

In most games, they go through periods where they lose focus. They never got going at all in this one. It’s extraordinary that Dujon Sterling might actually have won it at the death.

McInnes needs to take a degree of the blame himself, of course. Rangers had been scintillating against St Johnstone at the weekend when winning 4-0 and seeing their front four of Kevin Kelsy, Ryan Naderi, Kim Min-su and Badredine Bouanani light up Ibrox. Yes, Bouanani was taken off with cramp against Saints. There’s a cup semi against Aberdeen at the weekend as well. However, dropping the Algerian, moving Min-su out right and putting in Djeidi Gassama on the left didn’t work out at all.

Gassama was frankly awful. When he was taken off eight minutes into the second half, it wasn’t a moment too soon.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes shakes hands with Hearts' Wouter Vrancken at full-time

Nicolas Rankin battles for the ball with Hearts winger Calvin Miller

Rangers’ alarming slide from title contenders to no-marks under Danny Rohl last season showed that the one-time Sheffield Wednesday winger wasn’t up to it and, despite some decent contributions in recent months, that hasn’t changed.

This was a stark reminder of the need to replace him and other guys who had their chance at a championship crown last term and blew it. A real problem for Rangers throughout the match was the inability to get any kind of grip on midfield.

Dan Neil gave away a slack free-kick in a stupid area when tripping Tomas Magnusson to set up the home side’s first goal. Giving away needless fouls in daft areas was a constant issue.

However, Nico Raskin was much worse in the engine room. It remains unsettling that the transfer Brains’ Trust inside Auchenhowie couldn’t muster up a decent deal to sell the Belgian in the summer after he had been heavily involved in his country’s World Cup campaign.

Overall, Raskin has been a disappointment at Ibrox. He wants to move on and, if something can’t be put together in January, a buyer has to be found before next season. He cannot be part of the longer-term plan there.

Same goes for Emmanuel Fernandez. He got booked late in the first half for a brainless foul on Josh McPake and could have been yellow-carded earlier for a trip on Magnusson. The less said about his efforts at both of Hearts’ goals, the better. Mind you, Sterling was even worse at their second.

How Rangers can go from playing Celtic off the park twice in quick succession to the likes of this is quite the mystery.

Of course, there have been lots of changes in the playing staff of late in a bid to throw off the club’s ‘losers’ tag and it’s impossible to overturn the squad completely in one window.

However, carrying on with guys who were part of past failures is in danger of delivering failure again.

#1655. Man Utd sent Bruno Fernandes price tag warning as big-money club prepare fresh £45m January bid

By Lewis Blain | 02 Nov 2026 08:10, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 08:10

Manchester United could face a significant decision over Bruno Fernandes' future, with Al-Hilal reportedly preparing a fresh offer for their captain in January.

However, former Chelsea striker Tony Cascarino believes Premier League clubs would be unwilling to pay £60m for the Portuguese midfielder, raising questions over his market value.

With Fernandes' contract situation unresolved and growing doubts about his future at Old Trafford, a departure next year is increasingly plausible.

Al-Hilal have revived their interest in Fernandes and are prepared to offer €55m (£45m) as early as January.

That could provide United with an opportunity to cash in on their captain, whose contract is approaching its final months, although the club reportedly have an option to extend it by another year.

Cascarino, speaking on talkSPORT's Weekend Sports Breakfast, questioned whether any Premier League side would pay up to £60m for the 32-year-old.

He acknowledged Fernandes' importance to United over several seasons but argued that his age, wages and recent form would make such a fee difficult to justify for a domestic rival.

"You might from Saudi Arabia, but you wouldn't from another Premier League team - there is no way that would happen," Cascarino said.

Fernandes' relationship with Michael Carrick has also come under scrutiny after he questioned United's pressing approach following their 4-1 defeat to Como. He was subsequently dropped to on the bench against AFC Bournemouth before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea.

Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda believes the midfielder's time at Old Trafford is coming to an end.

Speaking to talkSPORT Breakfast, he suggested that a separation could benefit both Fernandes and United, arguing that the midfielder would have a better opportunity to compete for major honours at a more established club.

#1651. Liverpool are now cooking with gas under Andoni Iraola and will be firmly in Premier League title picture if they beat Arsenal as Jordan Henderson and Xabi Alonso leave Anfield with egg on their face, writes LEWIS STEELE

Published: 18:39 EDT, 28 October 2026 | Updated: 19:50 EDT, 28 October 2026

At times during a madcap night at a deceivingly cold Anfield, it felt like we were stuck in a fever dream.

There was Joe Gomez, a player who is yet to score a goal in professional football despite this being his 13th season, briefly morphing into prime Harry Kane to dispatch a penalty like he has been taking them all his life.

Just before, the Premier League and Champions League-winning captain Jordan Henderson was receiving deafening boos from the Kop in a bizarre chapter to the England midfielder’s once-illustrious Anfield career.

Henderson slotted his penalty home with confidence but still departed his old stomping ground with egg on his face, just like his manager Xabi Alonso. The Spaniard, who scored in the 2005 Champions League final for Liverpool, experienced an unhappy homecoming on Merseyside.

After a goal apiece just before half-time, from Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo, a tense battle had to be settled by penalties, with Liverpool No 2 goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili taking the plaudits for a fine save that was followed by a horrendous skied attempt from Wesley Fofana.

That was a true defender’s penalty after some thunderous spot-kicks beforehand, with Fofana’s effort going high into the Kop to leave Liverpool dancing and Alonso and Co cursing.

Liverpool reached the Carabao Cup quarter-finals after beating Chelsea 6-5 on penalties

Wesley Fofana sent the decisive spot kick miles over the bar after a dreadful effort

Giorgi Mamardashvili made a crucial stop from Emmanuel Emegha's penalty, which would have won the tie for Chelsea just before that

Iraola now has the chance of completing a double of sorts on Sunday when he takes on fellow old pal Mikel Arteta and Arsenal. It was at the Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea grassroots club in San Sebastian that Iraola, Alonso and Arteta played in the same team back in the 1990s.

Should Liverpool do what Fleetwood Town famously did and beat the Gunners, they will be firmly in the picture for the Premier League title as Iraola’s side are starting to build up a head of steam. After a slow start, Iraola’s team is now cooking on gas, this their fifth win on the spin.

But even if the league title is a step too far this season for this team in transition, there are tangible signs they are heading in the right direction and the body-language of players during the shoot-out showed they are taking every competition seriously.

Inside Anfield, it felt like everyone grew into the night and the desire to win grew with every passing minute. Virgil van Dijk, who was substituted, was living life like a fan with his arm around fellow old-timer Alisson.

Defender Ronald Araujo was on his haunches praying one second, the next leaping up and acting like a cheer-leader, as Dua Lipa’s One Kiss rang around Anfield after Fofana missed his kick. This win puts them closer to kissing the first trophy of the Iraola era.

Iraola was delighted as he not only managed to continue the eye-catching form and growing team spirit but simultaneously give a rest to key players. For a manager, that is the perfect cocktail.

‘Honestly, I was talking to (the press officer) and I said the only thing I wouldn’t want is Bournemouth (in the next round),’ said Iraola, smiling. ‘It is special but they know me very well – it is what it is, we are not lucky with the draw! We play Spurs, Chelsea and then Bournemouth.’

Asked on the team spirit, he added: ‘I feel (togetherness) and I am very happy to feel it, it is very important to me that we are feeling the support of the ones in the stands and a lot of the players have given us very good help and it is the third game at home we finish with good feelings.’

Chelsea also went 1-0 ahead from a penalty after Ryan Gravenberch fouled Moises Caicedo

Morgan Rogers made no mistake as he slotted home to score his fifth goal of the season

But Cody Gakpo equalised for Liverpool just three minutes later, also from the penalty spot

Alonso had few good feelings, as his side failed to capitalise on a significantly weakened Liverpool XI with seven changes from the weekend and £552million worth of talent sat on the bench.

With no Europe to fight for, the Chelsea manager’s chances of silverware in his first year have diminished.

At one point in a rather dull first half an hour, one wondered if the two managers would be best suited just shaking hands on a penalty shoot-out right there and then.

It seemed that was taken literally when two spot-kicks in three minutes breathed some life into the contest – and how refreshing it was to not have to watch 50 replays from every angle possible as the ghouls in Stockley Park microanalysed every single detail of the decisions.

First, Ryan Gravenberch tripped Moises Caicedo foolishly in the penalty area, when the Ecuadorian midfielder was not going anywhere. Rogers stepped up for the Blues and confidently sent Mamardashvili the wrong way.

The away end were in fine voice but they were soon brought crashing back to earth when the referee was pointing to the spot at the other end, as Virgil van Dijk’s attempted header clattered into the arm of Wesley Fofana. Gakpo, like Rogers a few minutes earlier, dispatched with ease.

Former Liverpool favourites Xabi Alonso and Jordan Henderson both returned to Anfield

Both goalkeepers put in fine displays for the rest of the game with Mike Penders atoning for his errors against Tottenham in the Chelsea goal. Mamardashvili, who also made big stops, was the one who had the last laugh, saving Emmanuel Emegha’s penalty in the bottom corner.

Liverpool have now played Chelsea in five shoot-outs and won every single one, including the 2022 FA Cup and Carabao Cup finals. Maybe another trip to Wembley will soon be on the cards for Iraola’s exciting team which is growing its team spirit by the week.

#1649. Barella admits Inter have changed derby approach in recent years: “We’re too inconsistent”

After the game, Nicolo Barella attempted to lessen the damage of last night’s loss to AC Milan in his post-game press conference.

For Milan, last night was another instance in what is becoming a new norm. After Inter’s streak of derby wins, it’s now the Rossoneri who are enjoying themselves. They’ve won each of their last four meetings and haven’t lost in eight games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In short, despite all of the managerial changes that have taken place, the Diavolo remain on top when it comes to playing the Nerazzurri.

Of course, last night’s win was also monumental considering what it meant for the Serie A table. Rather than falling 10 points behind, they only sit four points behind Inter and Lazio, who share first.

Speaking at a post-match conference, Barella admitted that Inter are going through a bad cycle in the derbies, but was keen to remember the streak from a few years ago, as MilanNews relayed.

“Certainly, if we talk about this, we’ve been lacking the ideal approach to matches since the start of the year. Right now, it’s a clear criticality for us.

“It’s true that we’ve shown our strength on many occasions, perhaps coming out on top in the second half or whenever we manage to break the deadlock, but it’s clear that not every match goes that way.

“We can’t expect to always repeat the same pattern, especially when we face a packed schedule with matches every three days. Fatigue, both physical and mental, is starting to take its toll, and we need to learn to manage matches better without being forced to keep them in the balance until the ninetieth minute.”

Is there a feeling that, whatever you do, Milan will prevail in derbies?

“Let’s say I’ve also experienced it the other way around. I’ve had a lot of derby wins in a row, so I don’t know if it’s a cyclical thing, but it’s definitely a game we haven’t approached in the best way in recent years, recently.

“There have been derbies where we’ve played well and lost, where we’ve played poorly and maybe drawn, but we’re too inconsistent in derbies, and right now, even in important matches. Even though we won, we still needed to do better.”

Do you still have the fierce desire to prove that you are the strongest?

“Being the strongest is sometimes not enough, because we’ve also been the strongest team, or the one everyone thought was the strongest, but then we didn’t win. So right now, I think we need to focus on something else rather than our strength.

“It’s true that if we look back at the last few games, many goals come from individual errors, and we need to improve on those, each of us, because unfortunately, individual errors work against the team. But as a team, we need to improve a bit in terms of solidity, which is what has always set us apart, what got us to the Champions League final, what helped us win the Scudetto, and perhaps right now we’re not the best version of ourselves. So we need to work on that. We still have the desire to win, for sure, because that’s what keeps us going to the pitch every day and motivates us, but we need to improve.”

#1648. Messi was a deity among Argentina’s unholy rabble

Little sorcerer calls time on playing for his country six weeks after World Cup final defeat which was marred by brutality of his team-mates

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could. Sobbing and desolate under a cloudless New Jersey sky, he understood that his last game for Argentina had also been among his worst.

Where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl. No wonder he stood apart while Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina did their worst, preferring to absorb one more chorus of adoration from the blue-and-white disciples before forsaking the stage for good.

You could make the case that Messi, as captain of an unholy rabble that had sought only to kick lumps out of Spain, should have taken a moral lead by hauling his team-mates into line, rather than reducing himself to their level by agitating to have Marc Cucurella sent off.

And yet for 20 years, the little sorcerer stayed aloof from his nation’s most lurid antics on the pitch, establishing himself as a strangely beatific presence on whom the highest ideals could be projected. Anybody who has heard Messi’s name being chanted by 50,000 fervent Argentines would have felt it. He was as close as 21st-century sport has come to a secular deity, the object of such veneration that Pope Francis felt compelled to remind Catholics that it was sacrilegious to keep calling him God.

Today, with one agonised announcement, that glorious delirium is over, and already Argentina seems not to know what to do with itself. Pablo Giralt, a sports anchor in Buenos Aires, was unable even to speak when he heard the news live on air, while shattered young fans described how they had called their parents in tears.

Everybody had known the moment was approaching, given the finality of his exit from the final and the subsequent death of his father, Jorge, but it still triggered an unbearable sense of loss.

Messi was the force who galvanised a nation, propelling his side from the unfathomable low of defeat to Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup to holding the trophy aloft 26 days later. Who could ever hope to emulate him, to detonate such joy that the team’s homecoming bus parade in the capital had to be abandoned for a helicopter ride because of the millions on the streets?

“Thank you, God, for making me Argentine,” Messi wrote in his earnest sign-off, his strength of allegiance unfailing to the end. As a veteran of 207 international matches, with his last at La Bombonera distinguished by an ecstatic ovation, he understood both the passions he unleashed among his people and the extent to which his own story became that of an entire country.

You struggled to imagine what life was like in the eye of this madness, with his every move stalked. For the wonder of Messi was that the cult went beyond borders, that the joy he inspired across six World Cups made him beloved to billions. An abiding memory of the 2022 final is of the walk back to the metro station in Doha, where thousands of Nepalese and Bangladeshi supporters, all part of the vast migrant workforce that had built the stadiums, united in “Messi, Messi” refrains even at 1am.

Messi was majestic at that tournament, so imperious in filleting Croatia in the semi-finals that Argentina’s TV reporters abandoned even the pretence of objectivity. “Truly, you made your mark in everyone’s life, and that to me is beyond winning any World Cup,” gushed Sofia Martinez of Television Publica. And when he won it all, the mark only deepened. To occupy any press box at the World Cup where Argentina were involved this summer was to see South American colleagues in “Messi 10” jerseys, helplessly in thrall to his greatness.

As a 39-year-old, he confounded every expectation, scoring a hat-trick against Algeria and breaking Miroslav Klose’s World Cup goals record. Even when engineering those implausible fightbacks against Egypt and England, he held a volatile team together with a minimum of fuss.

Lionel Messi: #FIFAWorldCup edition 🇦🇷🌟 pic.twitter.com/E2xOh3Iose

To study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

That alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pelé’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

#1647. Liverpool sour on star just months after record-breaking deal - opinion

Liverpool have soured on one star and it's just a matter of months since his record-breaking deal with the club. Can he turn things around?

Liverpool have struck many, many massive deals in the last 18 months. It's been quite ridiculous, really, as the spending is unlike anything we've ever seen at Anfield before.

They've broken their transfer record at least twice. Possibly three times depending on who you believe on the final price for Bradley Barcola. They certainly broke the British transfer record by signing Alexander Isak.

There were enormous new contracts for Mohamed Salah and Virgil van Dijk in 2025. And just the overall spend has been record-breaking. Again, we've not seen anything like it from Liverpool before.

But that isn't to say it's flawless. Far from it, actually. And one deal struck earlier this year now looks particularly poor.

Liverpool signed Ryan Gravenberch to a bumper new contract earlier this year. The total deal in salary was worth around £87m, per De Telegraaf, and we quickly called it a nightmare.

That's a situation that's continued, too. Gravenberch has struggled for over a year now, not just for form but to find a place in this Liverpool team that makes sense for him.

He's struggled as a holding player because he doesn't want to hold his position. He's struggled as more box-to-box player as he tends to get lost without a defined job. And he struggles as a no.10 because he just doesn't have the spacial awareness for it.

It's all come to a head. Liverpool went into a massive match at Anfield on Sunday against Arsenal and Gravenberch was not selected to start, instead finding himself behind a teenager in Trey Nyoni, a midfielder who wasn't given a new contract in Alexis Mac Allister, and a playmaker who hasn't quite proven himself in Florian Wirtz.

And it's important to remember that this was a record-breaking contract for Gravenberch. Liverpool have never paid a midfielder so much, even if we understand that Dominik Szoboszlai's subsequent contract was worth in the same range.

This wasn't the plan. It's been a little over six months since Gravenberch signed the deal and it was absolutely supposed to lock him down as the key midfielder in the side.

Instead, he can't get in the team and faces a real fight to win a place back. Liverpool - or at least, Andoni Iraola - has soured on him as a starting player and that really, really wasn't the plan.

#1646. England squad announcement: When will Thomas Tuchel confirm squad for November international break?

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 08:34, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 08:38

Thomas Tuchel’s England are back in action this month as they resume their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

After finishing third at this summer’s World Cup, the Three Lions won three of their opening four League A Group C fixtures across an 11-day period during the September/October international break.

England responded to their matchday one defeat at home to world champions Spain (3-2) by smashing Croatia 7-0 in between two more victories without reply against the Czech Republic.

With two more games on the horizon, Sports Mole runs through everything you need to know about England's latest squad announcement.

Tuchel will announce his England squad ahead of the upcoming international break at 10am on Friday, November 6.

The Three Lions boss is then expected to hold a press conference on the same day to explain the decisions he has made.

A 27-man squad was initially named by Tuchel in September, though a number of high-profile names eventually pulled out.

Six days after Tuchel's squad announcement, England will welcome Croatia to Wembley Stadium for their penultimate League A Group C fixture at 7.45pm on November 12.

The Three Lions will conclude their Nations League group with a trip to Riyadh Air Metropolitano – Atletico Madrid’s home stadium – where they will face Spain at 7.45pm (GMT) on November 15.

England currently sit second in League A Group C with nine points from their opening four matches, three behind leaders Spain who boast a 100% record.

The Three Lions also sit six points clear ahead of Croatia in third and know that either a draw or victory against the Checkered Ones would guarantee a top-two finish in the group.

The top-two teams in all four groups in League A will progress to the quarter-finals; Spain have already qualified with two games to spare but could still be pipped to top spot by England.

Group winners are seeded for the quarter-final draw, meaning they will be drawn against a runner-up from another group and will also host the second leg of their two-legged tie.

Meanwhile, England captain Harry Kane is set to return to international action for the first time since winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or.

Already the nation's all-time top scorer with 91 goals, Kane will aim to surpass Peter Shilton (125) to become England's most-capped men’s player in history.
